facts.text: Mixed motion occurs when both the machine and the person or vehicle are moving, requiring the system to predict where each will be rather than only where they are now.
facts.quote: Mixed motion is the case where both the machine and the person or vehicle are moving, so the system must predict where each will be, not just where they are now.

facts.text: Most collision tests use a stationary target or a target on a fixed path.
facts.quote: Most collision tests use a stationary target or a target on a fixed path

facts.text: Real-site mixed motion includes people stepping out from behind a stockpile, trucks reversing into a loading position while a loader swings, and dozers changing direction at a tip head.
facts.quote: real sites have people who step out from behind a stockpile, trucks that reverse into a loading position while a loader swings, and dozers that change direction at a tip head [Chapter 4]

facts.text: Collision decision logic for mixed motion must work with a predicted path.
facts.quote: The logic must therefore work with a predicted path.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 allows the risk area to be shaped by the machine's projected or expected path.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 allows the risk area to be shaped by the machine's "projected or expected path"

facts.text: The booklet's margin formula uses the predicted path distance R to the collision point.
facts.quote: the booklet's margin formula uses the predicted path distance R to the collision point [Chapter 8]

facts.text: The machine's own path is predictable from speed, steering and articulation, whereas the other party's path is not.
facts.quote: The machine's own path is predictable from speed, steering and articulation; the other party's is not

facts.text: A worker or another machine may react to the braking machine, changing the other party's motion.
facts.quote: a worker or another machine may also react to the braking machine [Chapter 7]

facts.text: Time to collision assumes straight-line closing and fails when motion is sideways, rotating or starting from rest.
facts.quote: Time to collision assumes straight-line closing and fails when motion is sideways, rotating or starting from rest [Chapter 8]

facts.text: University of Pretoria research samples plausible steering-rate trajectories to predict collisions and reduce false interventions; the initial results are simulation-only.
facts.quote: Research at the University of Pretoria samples plausible steering-rate trajectories to predict collisions and cut false interventions, with simulation-only initial results [Chapter 8]

facts.text: Validated off-road behavioral models of workers and equipment operators were not found, so simulated virtual-pedestrian movement is an assumption requiring its own validation.

facts.text: Mixed motion requires controlled whole-machine tests and cannot be delegated to an unvalidated model.
facts.quote: Mixed motion is listed among the controlled whole-machine tests that cannot be delegated to an unvalidated model [Chapter 1]

facts.text: Replay of recorded data cannot answer mixed-motion questions because, after braking acts, the recorded movements of other actors are no longer valid.

facts.text: Low-speed work needs comparatively large zones at blind corners and where people enter the machine's path from the side.
